purpose: Alternative wormhole hub architectural concepts for Stellar Syndicates

concepts.title: A — AUTHORITY NEXUS
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one new 2D concept-art painting for a WORMHOLE HUB in the dark sci-fi strategy game Stellar Syndicates. This is an early architectural design exploration, not a turnaround or modeling reference sheet.
Subject: a monumental orbital commercial station that stabilizes a wormhole and handles interstellar freight. A real, clearly visible circular traversable wormhole aperture is the focal point, with a tightly contained violet-indigo energy surface receding into a dark throat. Build the station around this open passage. No building, mast, bridge or reactor blocks the central aperture. The outer construction must unmistakably include useful cargo docks, empty ship berths, hangars or warehouses; this is a commercial transit hub.
Composition: one complete station only, a single elevated three-quarter view looking about 45 degrees down, with a roughly horizontal portal plane. Entire silhouette visible with at least 8 percent breathing room at every edge. Wide 3:2 landscape image. Quiet light neutral gray studio backdrop without scenery or a ground plane; sufficient shadow on the object to reveal depth. No starfield or surrounding objects. Soft upper-left key light, crisp silhouette, finely resolved construction detail.
Rendering: high-quality semi-realistic digital game concept art with convincing volumetric hard-surface forms, controlled painterly surface detail and architectural clarity. Designed so a 3D artist can understand the major masses. Keep large readable forms and a clear hierarchy, with selective fine detail. This is a materially new design direction; do not reuse a radial twelve-docking-finger silhouette.
Constraints: no detached ships, no people, no planets, no moons, no guns, no combat effects, no ornamental weapons, no screen interface, no crop, no watermark, no multiple views, no orbit diagram. Wormhole emission remains tightly contained rather than a halo obscuring hardware. Do not change the view to face a vertical circular gate. Only the specified small charcoal title below the object, no other text or logo.

DESIGN DIRECTION A — AUTHORITY NEXUS: a prestigious, orderly civic gateway combining monumental Art Deco architecture and elegant future engineering. A single broad concentric terraced disk surrounds the portal, with a six-sided outer footprint formed by huge stepped docking terraces, not narrow arms. Two low elegant symmetrical port halls stretch along the left and right edges, integrated beneath the terraces. Three evenly spaced sculptural fluted pylons rise from the outer perimeter, well outside the aperture, each a tapering streamlined buttress with subtle brass vertical fins, making an unmistakable monumental crown silhouette. Curved glass observation arcades, very fine warm window bands, sunken dark empty freight berths and broad pale cargo aprons. Pale ivory titanium and pearl ceramic cladding over dark graphite understructure, brushed brass ribs, quiet cyan navigation lights. Clean regulated prestige, immense but practical; no gothic spires and no religious motifs. Keep the portal open and clearly the central function.
Title verbatim: "A — AUTHORITY NEXUS".

DESIGN DIRECTION B — INDUSTRIAL FREEPORT: rugged utilitarian megastructure built for extreme freight throughput. A massive thick OCTAGONAL steel portal collar is clamped inside a broad asymmetrical RECTANGULAR cargo-station framework. The silhouette is angular and blocky, not circular with symmetric petals. Two enormous rectangular warehouse and drydock masses occupy opposite edges; one is long and low, the other stacked and tall. Deep open-sided freighter berths, oversized orange gantry cranes, heavy trusses and external utility pipelines, groups of freight containers, black inset radiator banks, hazard-striped loading edges. The violet wormhole remains a large clear circle in the middle of the rectangular infrastructure, not hidden inside a hangar. Machinery is bolted, repairable and weathered, with replaced panels and structural reinforcement. Charcoal iron, weathered gray steel, faded ochre-yellow and burnt-orange equipment, warm amber work lights. Broad deliberate shapes with strong negative spaces; no slender towers or ornamental architecture.
Title verbatim: "B — INDUSTRIAL FREEPORT".

DESIGN DIRECTION C — PRECURSOR EXCHANGE: an ancient mysterious alien gate repurposed into a commercial transit hub. THREE monumental smooth sweeping crescent-shaped buttresses, spaced evenly around a low circular gate collar, rise outward and then curve inward around the aperture without crossing it. They form a continuous physically connected sculptural architecture, not floating fragments. The central horizontal portal is open. Large simple negative spaces, elegantly curved asymmetric blade profiles on each buttress, heavy black obsidian-like ceramic with very subtle iridescent graphite panels, luminous hairline violet-cyan seams and restrained pale silver inlays. Architecture feels impossibly old and precise, not biological flesh. Contrasting compact human-built modular silver freight docks, boxy warehouse cuffs and tiny amber-lit cargo infrastructure are bolted neatly to the outside base of the ancient collar; they give scale and identify a working commercial station. Keep these docks visibly useful but subordinate to the three dramatic alien curves. Spacious, restrained and iconic; no swarm of small spikes, no clutter, no runes or writing, no disconnected pieces.
Title verbatim: "C — PRECURSOR EXCHANGE".

DESIGN DIRECTION D — SYNDICATE BAZAAR: a dense, lively independent merchant-city built around an immense open wormhole basin. The central containment torus is structurally clear, while its OUTER rim supports terraced clusters of stacked modular market buildings, habitation blocks and warehouses of many sizes. A tall asymmetrical cluster of broad rectangular skyscraper-like trade towers sits toward the back-left, balanced by much lower wide docks on the front-right, creating a distinctive city skyline rather than symmetric pylons or spokes. Buildings lean inward only slightly and must never obstruct the open circular aperture. Thick horizontal platforms project outward as empty freighter piers; practical container gantries, skybridges restricted to OUTSIDE the portal, exposed service pipes and a few large vertical radiator slabs. Weathered dark navy and muted teal painted metal with gray replacements, warm dense amber windows, restrained cyan and magenta illuminated architectural strips. Human, improvised, affluent in places and patched in others, believable trade infrastructure rather than a military fortress. Large readable skyline masses with selective detail, not a formless jumble. No textual billboards, no holographic ads, no fantasy roofs.
Title verbatim: "D — SYNDICATE BAZAAR".
